title: Finite sums of valuation-ring lattices with their subspace topology
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $J$ be a finite nonempty set. For each $j\in J$, let $\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$ be an $A$-submodule admitting an $A$-basis of $r$ vectors which is also an $E$-basis of $E^r$. Put $\Lambda=\sum_{j\in J}\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$, and equip these modules with the subspace topology from the product topology on $E^r$. Then $\Lambda$ admits an $A$-basis of $r$ vectors which is an $E$-basis of $E^r$. For every such basis the coordinate map $A^r\to\Lambda$ is a homeomorphism, and the same holds for each $\Lambda_j$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (more-algebra-lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3); topology calculation expanded from the blueprint trace paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a discrete valuation ring and $E$ is its fraction field. Choose an $A$-basis $v_{j,1},\ldots,v_{j,r}$ of each $\Lambda_j$. Their finite union generates $\Lambda$: expanding each summand in its basis expresses every element of the sum as an $A$-linear combination of this union. The submodule $\Lambda\subseteq E^r$ is torsion-free: if $0\ne a\in A$ and $ax=0$, multiply in $E^r$ by $a^{-1}$ to get $x=0$. Choose $j_0\in J$. Since $\Lambda_{j_0}\subseteq\Lambda$ and the $v_{j_0,i}$ form an $E$-basis, $\Lambda$ spans $E^r$.

source.place: Local computation, second paragraph: finitely generated torsion-free module containing a full lattice

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] to $R=A$ and $M=\Lambda$. Step 1 verifies both finite generation and torsion-freeness, and the coefficient ring is a DVR. Obtain a finite $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $\Lambda$.

source.place: Local computation, second paragraph: finitely generated torsion-free, hence free

proof.text: This $A$-basis is an $E$-basis of $E^r$. It spans because every element of $\Lambda$ is an $A$-linear combination of the $b_i$, and Step 1 gives $E\Lambda=E^r$. For independence, write any relation $\sum_i c_i b_i=0$ with $c_i\in E$ as $c_i=a_i/s_i$, where $a_i,s_i\in A$ and $s_i\ne0$, using the fraction-field assertion of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Put $s=\prod_i s_i\ne0$. Multiplication by $s$ gives an $A$-linear relation with coefficients $sc_i\in A$. Independence over $A$ gives $sc_i=0$, hence $c_i=0$. By the equality of finite basis cardinalities in [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], this basis and the standard basis of $E^r$ have the same size, so $n=r$. Relabel the basis accordingly.

source.place: Local computation, second paragraph: spans E^r, hence a lattice of rank r; fraction-field and rank details expanded

proof.text: Let $N$ be either $\Lambda$ or one of the $\Lambda_j$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be any $A$-basis of $N$ that is also an $E$-basis of $E^r$. Consider the $E$-linear equivalence $B:E^r\to E^r$, $B(x)=\sum_i x_i b_i$. The field $E$ is complete for the absolute value in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and that norm is nontrivial because $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$. The product topology on $E^r$ is Hausdorff and makes it a finite-dimensional topological $E$-vector space: operations are continuous coordinatewise. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] makes $B$ and $B^{-1}$ continuous.

source.place: Local computation, second paragraph: basis identification with the valuation-ring power; topology made explicit

proof.text: The equality $B(A^r)=N$ is exactly the assertion that the chosen $b_i$ are an $A$-basis. Restrict the mutually inverse continuous maps from Step 4 to $A^r$ and $N$. They remain continuous for the induced topologies. The topology induced on $A^r\subseteq E^r$ is precisely the product of the subspace topologies on $A\subseteq E$: a basic product open restricts to $\prod_i(U_i\cap A)$, and every basic product open of $A^r$ has that form. On $N$ the induced topology is the topology specified in the statement. These restrictions are therefore the required mutually inverse homeomorphisms for every such basis, both for $\Lambda$ and for each $\Lambda_j$. When $r=0$, all modules are zero, the bases are empty, and these maps are maps between one-point spaces.
